title: Traffic shaper & safety heuristics for automated batching/caching recommendations
creator: Asha Rao
description: Objective: Automate batching and KV-prefix caching recommendations while guaranteeing latency and throughput SLOs via a lightweight traffic shaper and anomaly-aware rollback. This ticket builds the safety layer that (1) constrains automated config applies with runtime-aware limiters, (2) routes traffic across model variants and capacity tiers in an SLO-aware way, and (3) detects anomalies to trigger safe rollback or traffic quarantine. Deliverables: recommender adapter, staged apply controller, SLO-aware router, anomaly detector, dashboards and runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Recommender outputs candidate batching/cache profiles that include expected latency/throughput delta and confidence score
Controller can stage a config change to a canary cohort and apply/retract within 60s via orchestrated API
Traffic shaper enforces per-cohort token rate and inflight limits; measured p99 latency for canary cohort must not exceed baseline+p99_delta_threshold
Anomaly detector triggers automatic rollback when latency/error/throughput divergences exceed configured detection window and confidence
Operational dashboard (cost vs latency) shows before/after, and on-call runbook documents manual override and emergency kill-switch
End-to-end integration test simulates a config apply and validates rollback on injected latency spike
tech_notes: We will extend the recommender to emit 'safety metadata' (expected p50/p90/p99 impact, traffic sensitivity, and sample rate) rather than opaque suggestions
Staged apply controller will use incremental cohorts: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with time and SLO gates at each step
Limiters: per-cohort max_inflight, token_rate cap, per-host concurrency cap. Defaults are conservative and exposed for tuning via runtime-config
Routing: SLO-aware router evaluates real-time SLO signals (p99_latency, error_rate, throughput) and will divert to fallback model variant or higher-tier capacity when thresholds breached
Anomaly detection uses two streams: fast (1m windows, EWMA drift) for immediate failures and slow (15m windows, nonparametric change-point detection) for regressions. Both produce a confidence score
Rollback policy: automatic rollback if anomaly confidence > 0.95 and metric delta exceeds configured absolute/relative bounds for at least N consecutive windows
Observability: add per-cohort and per-config tags to existing latency and cost metrics; create cost-latency scatter and timeline in Console
Safety-first UX: Console will show 'predicted risk' and a single-click pause/rollback. Default is require explicit opt-in for fully automated rollouts in customer accounts
